scope: All 28 historical public synthetic workloads. Direct native Rust engine, direct GNU grep, and direct rg; no Bash, Node compatibility wrapper or postprocessor in any child command. Full process startup and stdout/stderr pipe capture are timed. Warm-cache results are specific to this machine and these inputs.

methodology.timersInclude: spawn, complete child execution, process startup, complete stdout/stderr pipe capture
methodology.timersExclude: fixture construction, route report, inventory verification, output hashes, record sorting, semantic comparisons, report writing
methodology.GNUComparison: An independent untimed direct GNU oracle is compared against every timed observation: status, stdout and stderr. Rust must retain exact GNU bytes and order.
methodology.rgComparison: All full LF-delimited output records are compared as a byte multiset, preserving duplicates and line/count/file contents. File inventory, status and stderr must agree. Output order is explicitly reported; speed ratios are null for incompatible or unavailable observations.
methodology.timingBoundary: Python monotonic timer directly surrounds child creation and complete pipe capture/wait. Python startup, JSON encoding/decoding and Node orchestration are outside the timer.

semanticLimits: These 28 historical classes contain no PCRE pattern. GNU -P and rg --pcre2 have different syntax/defaults and are not qualified or timed here. No PCRE speed claim follows from these ERE/fixed-pattern rows.

rg uses explicit GNU-like hidden/ignore, byte encoding, C-locale case/word handling, filename prefixes and zero counts. Its default Unicode, ignore filtering and encoding detection are not being compared against GNU C semantics.
rg may emit equivalent complete records in a different order. Those ratios measure equivalent result records but not GNU output-order compatibility.
GNU binary diagnostic formatting/channel differs from rg. That row retains timings and hashes but does not receive a compatible-output speed ratio.
GNU -z count output ends with LF; rg --null-data count output ends with NUL. That row retains timings and hashes but does not receive a compatible-output speed ratio.
Historical class names ending in native are identifiers, not proof of the Rust route. Only the separate route evidence identifies native execution or GNU fallback.

fixture.materialization: Independent regular files with original contents; one large auxiliary group at a time. No sparse files, hardlinks, or reflinks.
fixture.cleanup: Owned temporary directory removed in finally after the report is written.
